note: Rule text is written by this project. standardRefs carry identifiers only — an identifier is a fact, the surrounding text is not. See NOTICE.

rules.title: Container runs as root by default
rules.rationale: With no USER instruction the image's processes start as uid 0. Anything that escapes a process then starts from the most privileged account inside the container, and any host directory mounted in is written as root.
rules.remediation: Create an unprivileged account in the image and end the Dockerfile with USER. If the process needs a low port, publish a high one instead of binding a privileged one as root.

rules.title: Environment variable looks like a credential
rules.rationale: A value baked into the image environment travels with every copy of that image and is readable by anyone who can reach the daemon. An image layer cannot be un-published.
rules.remediation: Pass the value at run time and rebuild without it. Rotate anything already pushed — deleting a tag does not delete the layer that held it.

rules.title: Image declares no health check
rules.rationale: Without a health check the runtime knows only that the process is alive, not that it works. A container serving nothing but errors stays "running" and keeps receiving traffic.
rules.remediation: Add a HEALTHCHECK that exercises the path the service actually serves, rather than only proving a port is open.

rules.title: Image exposes a port below 1024
rules.rationale: Ports under 1024 traditionally need privilege to bind, which pushes an image towards running as root. The exposure itself is harmless; the reason it is usually there is not.
rules.remediation: Listen on a high port inside the container and map it on the host, for example -p 80:8080.

rules.title: Build step uses ADD where COPY would do
rules.rationale: ADD also fetches URLs and unpacks archives, which turns a file copy into something that can pull in content the build never reviewed.
rules.remediation: Use COPY for local files. Fetch remote content in a RUN step so the download and its checksum are visible in the build.

rules.title: Image has an unusually large number of layers
rules.rationale: Every layer is a snapshot that keeps whatever the next step deleted. A long chain usually means removed files are still being shipped — including files removed because they were secret.
rules.remediation: Combine related RUN steps and use a multi-stage build so only the final artefacts reach the shipped image.

rules.title: Image has no digest to pin to
rules.rationale: Without a repository digest there is no way to ask for exactly this image again. A deployment elsewhere gets whatever the tag points at that day.
rules.remediation: Push the image to a registry and refer to it as name@sha256:… wherever it is deployed.

rules.title: Image is referenced by a moving tag
rules.rationale: A tag names a position, not an image. Two machines pulling on different days run different software while reporting the same version.
rules.remediation: Tag releases with an immutable version and deploy by digest.

rules.title: Image does not record where it came from
rules.rationale: Without a source or revision label, an image found on a machine cannot be traced to the commit that built it — the first question asked once it turns out to be vulnerable.
rules.remediation: Set org.opencontainers.image.source and org.opencontainers.image.revision at build time.

rules.title: Image was built more than 90 days ago
rules.rationale: Base images receive package updates continuously, so an image that has not been rebuilt cannot contain fixes published since it was built — however clean today's scan looks.
rules.remediation: Rebuild on a schedule so patched base layers are picked up, then scan again.

rules.title: Image was built more than 180 days ago
rules.rationale: Half a year of published fixes are missing from this image by construction. Its scan result describes the day it was built, not today.
rules.remediation: Rebuild from a current base image and scan again.

rules.title: Image was built more than a year ago
rules.rationale: A year without a rebuild means the base distribution has moved on, and some of what is inside may no longer receive fixes at all.
rules.remediation: Rebuild from a supported base image, or replace the image if its base has reached end of life.
